{{nihongo|'''Murakuni Masumida Shrine'''|村国真墨田神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kakamigahara|Q641491|qid=Q641491}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed shrine}}, and is regarded as the tutelary shrine of the {{ill|Unuma|ja|鵜沼町|ko|우누마정|qid=Q11675738|lt=Unuma area}} of Kakamigahara. It is one of the five {{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592}} shrines in Kakamigahara City. {{nihongo|'''Murakuni Masumida Shrine'''|村国真墨田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

== Overview ==
The founding period is around the 7th century. It is said that the local ruling {{ill|Gōzoku|Q84066|qid=Q84066}} {{ill|Murakuni Clan|ja|村国氏|qid=Q11523054}} of this area ({{ill|Mino Province|ckb|پارێزگای مینۆ|cs|Mino (provincie)|de|Provinz Mino|es|Provincia de Mino|eu|Mino probintzia|fa|ولایت مینو|fr|Province de Mino|gl|Provincia de Mino|hak|Mî-nùng-koet|id|Provinsi Mino|it|Mino (provincia)|ja|美濃国|ko|미노국|lt|Mino žemė|nl|Mino (provincie)|pt|Província de Mino|ru|Мино (провинция)|simple|Mino Province|sk|Mino (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мино|th|แคว้นมิโนะ|tr|Mino (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Міно|vi|Tỉnh Mino|wuu|美濃国|zh|美濃國|zh_min_nan|Mino-kok|zh_yue|美濃國|qid=Q864156}}, {{ill|Kakami district|Q11412369|qid=Q11412369}}) founded the shrine by jointly enshrining the main deity of {{ill|Nangū Taisha|Q704967|qid=Q704967}}, Mino Province {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}, "{{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|es|Kanayamahiko y Kanayamahime|ja|金山彦神|pl|Kanayamahiko|zh|金山毘古神|qid=Q4387856|lt=Kanayamahiko-no-Mikoto}}," with the main deity of Owari Province ichinomiya {{ill|Masumida Shrine|Q705916|qid=Q705916}}, {{ill|Amenohoakari|fr|Ame-no-hoakari|it|Amenohoakari|ja|天火明命|ko|아메노호아카리|mni|ꯑꯃꯦꯅꯣꯍꯣꯑꯀꯔꯤ|simple|Ame-no-hoakari|zh|天火明命|qid=Q10940411}}. Later, {{ill|Murakuni Oyori|fa|ماروکونی اویوری|ja|村国男依|qid=Q6937264}} was also enshrined as a principal deity<ref>On the plaque "Worship trestle of Engishiki Shikinaisha, Gifu Prefecture Kimpesha Murakuni Masumida Shrine," it is written that Murakuni no Oyori was enshrined as deity after death in praise of his achievements, and that Kanayamahiko-no-Mikoto and Ame-no-Hoakari-no-Mikoto were combined afterward.</ref>.

At the time of foundation, it is said to have stood about 500 meters south of the present site (along today's {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}}), where a temporary shrine site now remains. In the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}, during the {{ill|Eikyō|Q1193059|qid=Q1193059}} era ({{ill|1429|Q6326|qid=Q6326}}-{{ill|1440|Q6384|qid=Q6384}}), Ōsawa Toshiharu, a retainer of the {{ill|Toki clan|Q687635|qid=Q687635}}, built {{ill|Unuma Castle|Q11675737|qid=Q11675737}}; Murakuni Masumida Shrine became the guardian shrine of the Ōsawa family and was moved to the castle town of Unuma Castle.

In {{ill|1564|Q6632|qid=Q6632}} ({{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} 7), {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} ordered {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550|lt=Kinoshita Tokichiro}} to attack Unuma Castle and {{ill|Igiyama Castle|Q11379405|qid=Q11379405}}. Because of resistance by lord Ōsawa Jirōzaemon, the castle was difficult to capture. However, through Tokichiro's diplomacy Ōsawa yielded, and Unuma Castle was surrendered. Afterward Unuma Castle came under {{ill|Ikeda Tsuneoki|Q1036482|qid=Q1036482}}, lord of {{ill|Inuyama Castle|Q1155484|qid=Q1155484}}. After Tsuneoki's transfer, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nakagawa Sadanari}} became lord of Inuyama Castle, and Unuma Castle remained its subordinate.

In {{ill|1584|Q6728|qid=Q6728}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 12), during the {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|Q1353633|qid=Q1353633}}, Ikeda Tsuneoki used Unuma Castle as a base in operations against Inuyama Castle. Kawamura So-roku, who cooperated in that operation, obtained permission from {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550|lt=Hashiba Hideyoshi}} and relocated Murakuni Masumida Shrine from the Unuma castle town to its current site.

On September 25, {{ill|1973|Q2477|qid=Q2477}} (Showa 48), it was designated by Gifu Prefectural Shrine Office as a prefectural office chief worship-designated shrine ({{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592}}), designation No. Kin-71{{sfn|Kimura|1997|p=75}}.

It is one of the five Kimpesha shrines in Kakamigahara.

Its parishioners are the ten neighborhoods of the {{ill|Unuma|ja|鵜沼町|ko|우누마정|qid=Q11675738|lt=Unuma area}} ({{ill|Kawasaki|Q131870096|qid=Q131870096|lt=Kawasaki}}, {{ill|Mitsuike|Q131912299|qid=Q131912299|lt=Mitsuike}}, {{ill|Nishi-cho|Q131870135|qid=Q131870135|lt=Nishi-cho}}, {{ill|Higashi-cho|Q131870137|qid=Q131870137|lt=Higashi-cho}}, {{ill|Minami-cho|Q131870134|qid=Q131870134|lt=Minami-cho}}, {{ill|Yamazaki|ja|鵜沼山崎町|qid=Q131870129|lt=Yamazaki}}, {{ill|Hoshakuji|Q131912297|qid=Q131912297|lt=Hoshakuji}}, {{ill|Furuichiba|Q131912296|qid=Q131912296|lt=Furuichiba}}, {{ill|Koigi|Q131912294|qid=Q131912294|lt=Koigi}}, {{ill|Oigi|Q131912298|qid=Q131912298|lt=Oigi}})<ref name="村国真墨田神社">Plaque of Engishiki Shikinaisha Gifu Prefecture Kimpesha Murakuni Masumida Shrine</ref>.

== Main rituals<ref name="村国真墨田神社"/> ==
* January 1 - New Year festival
* {{ill|Vernal Equinox Day|Q1049141|qid=Q1049141}} - Kinen Festival and Masumida Inari Shrine festival
* Last Sunday of July - Summer purification festival
* August 15 - Unuma Gokoku Shrine spirit-comforting rite
* Second Sunday of October - Annual festival
* Mid-November - Niiname Festival
* December 31 - New Year's Eve festival
* First day of every month - Monthly festival

== Address ==
* 1-108 Unuma Yamazaki-cho, Kakamigahara, Gifu Prefecture
